A Ground-First Machine

The WR2 is unusually involved here — 19% of targets (league ~15%), meaning there's bankable volume beyond the top receiver.

The Offensive Blueprint

Their run game attacks the perimeter — 31% of carries hit the edge (league ~25%), an outside-zone lean that rewards speed backs and can boom for chunk gains.

They're a heavy under-center team (61% shotgun vs ~68%) — a pro-style, run-committed structure.

When they fall behind they abandon the run entirely — 58% pass while trailing, so their pass-catchers have huge comeback-script ceilings.

They play fast — 64 snaps a game (league ~61), and the extra volume is a rising tide that lifts everyone's counting stats.

In the Red Zone

Their red-zone identity is run-first (52% pass), funnelling touchdown equity to the lead back.

Defense — Soft on the Ground

They surrender 134 rushing and 239 passing yards per game (league ~120 / ~230). The run moves against them — target opposing RB1s.

They give up deep shots (21% of throws travel 15+ vs ~19%) — big-play WR upside against them.

They leak RB rushing TDs (0.56/game vs ~0.46) — an anytime-TD spot to attack.

They leak WR1 receiving TDs (0.47/game vs ~0.38) — an anytime-TD spot to attack.

The Betting Angles

Bottom line: back their RB1's rushing volume in favored/positive scripts; their pass-catchers have massive ceilings in comeback scripts (fade-material as underdogs); opposing RB1s smash on the ground and at the goal line.

Built on 2024–25 data; the profile rebuilds through the season as the current staff and roster set their own tendencies.
